Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call today — good to meet the Finova team. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align the next steps with your procurement/security timelines.

What I heard as your high-level decision criteria:
- Latency: user-facing chat flows — sub-second intent; looking for p95 and p99 targets to be explicit
- Cost: need clear unit economics and pricing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) to compare to current vendor
- Deployment mode: preference for a private VPC deployment (data residency + customer-managed networking) but open to dedicated reserved capacity if it meets security controls
- SLA / compliance: SOC2 + contract-level uptime / p99 targets; security team will run a short questionnaire and likely require a pen-test schedule

Clarifying questions (can you confirm / fill in):
1) Exact latency targets you want us to bid against (p95 / p99). You mentioned “fast”; can you share numbers?
2) Cost target (either absolute or relative to current spend) — is there a % reduction target you need to hit?
3) Deployment preference: is Private (VPC) mandatory for the pilot/prod, or is Dedicated with private networking acceptable?
4) Procurement timeline & next contact: who owns the PO/contract (procurement@finova.com?) and target close date?

Next steps from our side: I’ll pull together a short one-page comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private with typical p95/p99 numbers and unit costs for the model class we discussed, and a short SLA summary. I’m attaching the SLA summary and deployment one-pager for reference.

Proposed immediate next actions:
- You confirm the latency and cost targets and procurement owner (this email answers will work)
- We schedule a 30m tech sync with your security lead (SarahLee?) to run through the questionnaire
- We deliver a draft commercial proposal within 3 business days after we get confirmed targets and procurement contact

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Subject: Re: Decision criteria (latency / cost / SLA) - technical notes

Hi all — thanks for the context. A few technical clarifications from Redwood’s infra side to make sure the proposal is sized correctly:

1) Latency by deployment mode (typical ranges, p99, single-turn chat, ~2k token context):
   - Hosted (shared / multi-tenant): p95 ~120-260ms, p99 ~220-480ms (varies by model family and active QPS)
   - Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): p95 ~100-220ms, p99 ~180-350ms
   - Private (customer VPC / on-prem): similar to Dedicated when using the same HW; network egress/ingress and peering can add 10-80ms depending on region and topology

2) Key sizing inputs we need for an accurate proposal:
   - Expected sustained qps during business hours (avg and peak)
   - Average sequence length (tokens per request) for the interactive flows
   - Percent of requests that will hit cached prefixes / reranking vs full model run

3) SLA considerations:
   - Our standard SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% availability with a p99 latency target in the commercial appendix (we can negotiate higher SLA with committed reserved capacity and an on-call escalation path)
   - For Private/VPC deployments we provide the same SLOs but contracts need a network-level attachment schedule because we don’t manage customer network appliances

4) Cost levers: batching, quantization, and KV prefix caching significantly reduce per-token cost. If Finova can commit to a reserved capacity profile, we can provide stepped pricing that reaches your ~30% opex reduction target in many comparable deals.

Action items for Finova to help us finalize the offer:
- Provide qps and avg token length (best-effort)
- Confirm preferred model family (we discussed open-weights Llama-family equivalent in the call)

I’ll produce a short technical appendix and cost model to attach to the commercial proposal; Marissa will circulate the full doc next.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
